episode_title: Rebooting Hiring: Why Recruiters Must Become Business Partners | Katrina Collier

real_qa.q: Why did Katrina Collier write Reboot Hiring and what is its main purpose?
real_qa.r: Katrina Collier wrote Reboot Hiring as a companion to her first book, The Robot Proof Recruiter, to address the problem from the company leadership side. The book is designed for anyone in talent acquisition to hand to company leaders to make the case for them, arguing that leaders should partner properly with TA teams rather than treating them as a shared service. As she states, Reboot Hiring demonstrates to business leaders how to work with TA professionals effectively to save time, money, and hassle in hiring.

real_qa.q: What is Steve Levy's question that Katrina Collier recommends recruiters use in intake meetings?
real_qa.r: Steve Levy's recommended question is: 'How do you know at the end of 12 months you've hired the right person?' This question is powerful because most hiring managers have not been trained in leadership and development, and asking this forces them to articulate the real success criteria beyond the job description, including behaviors, skills, and outcomes they actually need.
real_qa.requete: Steve Levy 12 months hired right person question

real_qa.q: How does the recruitment alignment meeting or intake strategy session impact hiring success according to Katrina Collier?
real_qa.r: Katrina Collier emphasizes that the recruitment alignment meeting—also called the intake strategy session—is absolutely everything in the hiring process. This is where recruiters must go in with the attitude of being a business partner, not a service provider, asking strategic questions that make hiring managers think, and uncovering the real business problems and success criteria that the job needs to solve rather than relying on generic job descriptions.
real_qa.requete: recruitment alignment meeting intake strategy session importance

real_qa.q: Why do misconceptions about brand attracting talent actually represent a shift to reputation in hiring according to Reboot Hiring?
real_qa.r: Katrina Collier argues that while brand can attract talent, the real driver is now reputation, especially with reviews visible online. If a company has toxic leadership or poor employee reviews, even prestigious brands like Apple cannot attract top talent. The power has shifted to candidates who can see company reputation through platforms like Google, Indeed, and Glassdoor before they apply, so genuine company culture matters more than brand name.
real_qa.requete: brand vs reputation talent attraction online reviews

real_qa.q: What problem with AI-generated resumes has Katrina Collier identified since publishing Reboot Hiring?
real_qa.r: Katrina Collier reports that job seekers are using AI tools like Claude to make their resumes match job descriptions exactly, resulting in resumes that all look identical to the job posting and to each other. This makes it harder for recruiters to identify who is actually right for the role. She also noted that AI can introduce bias—when the same resume was submitted under different names (Jennifer vs. Jeff), Claude used different language, downplaying a woman's achievements while amplifying a man's for the same project.
real_qa.requete: AI resumes Claude identical job description bias

guest.titre: Keynote Speaker on Future Proofing Recruiters and TA
guest.bio_context: Katrina Collier has worked in recruitment for over 20 years across agency and in-house roles, and as a trainer. Since the publication of The Robot Proof Recruiter in 2019, she has focused primarily on speaking, facilitation, and writing. She has spoken at leading HR and recruitment conferences worldwide and works with talent acquisition teams globally, focusing on improving human connection in hiring processes.
